description: A split image. Left side: Hot, dry sand dunes of the modern Sahara. Right side: The same landscape but lush, green, and full of grass and lakes.
text_content: Imagine standing in the Sahara desert. Today, it is hot and sandy. But if you could travel back in time, you would see something amazing.

description: A prehistoric scene of the 'Green Sahara'. A lake with hippos, and people fishing in dug-out canoes. Giraffes grazing in the background.
text_content: Thousands of years ago, the Sahara was green! It was a land of flowing rivers, splashing hippos, and tall giraffes. People lived there happily.

description: A close-up of ancient rock art on a sandstone cave wall, depicting cattle and hunters. A hand of a modern child is reaching out to touch it (implied).
text_content: These people were the children of Phut. They painted pictures on the rocks of the animals they saw. We can still see these paintings today.

description: A time-lapse style composite showing the landscape transitioning from green savanna to dry scrubland, and finally to desert dunes. The mood is melancholic.
text_content: Slowly, the rain stopped falling. The grass turned brown. The lakes dried up. The sand took over. The people had to move.

description: Ancient engineers digging a 'foggara' tunnel in the desert rock. Water flows through a stone channel, irrigating a small oasis garden.
text_content: Some people learned to live in the desert. They were called the Garamantes. They dug deep tunnels to find water hidden underground.

description: A caravan of camels walking through a sandstorm, carrying goods. The riders are wrapped in indigo cloth. The sun is a hazy ball of white.
text_content: They rode horses and chariots across the sands. Later, they used camels. The camel was the 'ship of the desert' that helped them trade.

description: The ancient harbor of Carthage. It is circular and filled with wooden warships (triremes). The city rises white and majestic in the background.
text_content: On the coast, huge ships arrived. The Phoenicians built a great city called Carthage. It was famous for its purple cloth and mighty ships.

description: A dramatic scene of Hannibal’s army crossing the snowy Alps. War elephants are tramping through the snow, soldiers bracing against the wind.
text_content: Carthage became powerful. But a city called Rome wanted to be the boss. They fought huge wars. A general named Hannibal even rode elephants over mountains!

description: An Amazigh family in a mountain village, wearing traditional wool cloaks. They look proud and resilient. Roman ruins are visible in the far distance.
text_content: In the end, Rome won. But the people of Phut—the Amazigh—stayed strong. They kept their own language and their own ways.

description: A simple early Christian meeting in a North African home. Light streams in from a window. People are listening intently to a reader.
text_content: God had a plan for these tough people. Soon, the news of Jesus would come to their cities and farms, and they would become heroes of the faith.

description: A lone tree standing in the desert (an acacia), symbolizing resilience. The sun is setting, painting the sky in deep purples and oranges.
text_content: The desert may remain, but the history of the Green Sahara reminds us that the world is always changing in God's hands.

description: A parchment map of North Africa. It shows the Atlas Mountains and the Mediterranean coast. A dot for 'Carthage' and symbols for 'Oases' in the desert.
text_content: Map: The Changing Land. This map shows North Africa. The green spots show where the oasis cities were. Carthage is on the coast.
